stories.headline: Odisha ramps up cyclone evacuations
stories.title: Odisha ramps up cyclone evacuations
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its latest bulletin, said a depression over the Bay of Bengal moved southwestwards during the past six hours and intensified into a deep depression.
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: A brewing cyclone in the Bay of Bengal, expected to intensify three times over as a very severe cyclone, threatens to unleash a spell of dangerous weather across the South Peninsula, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20 cm forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, and Kerala and Mahe.
Isolated to extremely heavy rainfall is likely also over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Tuesday and Wednesday; and Telangana on Wednesday.
Heavy to very heavy rain (7-11 cm) is likely at isolated places over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe, and South Interior Karnataka.
Heavy rain at isolated places over Rayalaseema and Coastal Karnataka.
The bigger threat lies along the Andhra Pradesh coast, where the storm may make landfall by Wednesday.

Squally weather, gale-force winds and rough to very rough seas are forecast over the western and central Bay of Bengal from Tuesday, with impact spilling over to the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining Odisha coasts.

Sunday morning’s parent depression intensified into a deep depression and lay centred at over the same region about 420 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 870 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 960 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 1060 km east- Southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1,130 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).
It is very likely to move nearly southwest, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal early on Sunday morning.
Then it is very likely to move west-northwest over east-central and adjoining west-central Bay and intensify into a severe cyclone over west-central Bay by Tuesday morning.
Thereafter, it is very likely to move north-west, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach west-central Bay near Andhra Pradesh coast around Wednesday morning.

It is very likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclone with maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 km/hr gusting to 140 km/hr by Tuesday midnight/Wednesday morning.
The IMD has also warned of dangerous sailing/fishing conditions over the Bay waters over next few days.

article_sentences: Hyderabad: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Hyderabad Centre, has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy downpours likely in several Telangana districts bordering Andhra Pradesh on October 29.

According to IMD officials, a red alert has been issued for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam and Mahabubabad districts, where heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy falls, is likely.
An orange alert has been issued for Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Warangal, Suryapet, Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool districts, where heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places.

Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 50-60 kmph are likely in Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda districts.
Thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph are expected in the remaining districts.
Temperatures are likely to fall across Telangana over the next week, officials said.
Meanwhile, the IMD issued a bulletin on the severe cyclonic system over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal.

The system was located about 450 km north-northwest of Sri Vijayapuram in the Andaman Islands, 820 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 910 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 1,010 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam and 1,080 km east of Bapatla.
The system is likely to move westwards and intensify into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal in the early hours of October 26.
It is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by the morning of October 27.
The system may further intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of October 28.
The cyclone is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam from the morning to early afternoon of October 28.

stories.headline: Delhi building collapse: 2 feared trapped
stories.title: Delhi building collapse: 2 feared trapped
stories.summary: New Delhi, Two men, aged 60 and 36, are suspected to be trapped under the rubble after a slab of a house under construction collapsed in northeast Delhi's Harsh Vihar area on Sunday, prompting a rescue operation involving the NDRF, fire services and police, officers said.The incident took place in Milan Garden, triggering panic in the locality as the structure came crashing down. Rescue teams were clearing the debris and making efforts to ascertain whether the two men were trapped underneath, a senior police officer said.The Delhi Fire Services and police received information about the incident around 7 pm and rushed to the spot. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), the local police and the fire department were also engaged in the rescue and relief operation.A team from the Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) also reached the site and joined the efforts, the officer said."During local inquiries, we learnt that two people who were working at the building may be trapped under the rubble. One is a 60-year-old man and the other is 36. Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable," the officer said."Our main focus is to clear all the debris and, if someone is trapped, rescue them quickly," he added.The officer said construction work was underway on the first floor of the building when the house collapsed. However, the exact cause of the incident is yet to be ascertained.As the rescue operation progressed, no one had been found under the debris till the time of filing this report. Officials said the possibility of people being trapped had not yet been confirmed, and teams were continuing efforts to clear the rubble and assess the situation.Some family members of the two men alleged that the rescue work was progressing slowly and said they were attempting to remove the debris themselves in the hope of locating their relatives.Police personnel were deployed in strength at the site to maintain law and order and manage the crowd gathered near the collapsed structure. Emergency responders were coordinating their efforts to clear the debris safely and determine whether anyone remained trapped.The collapse drew a large number of local residents to the spot, with anxious family members waiting for information about the two men.Officials said the immediate priority was to clear the debris and establish whether the missing men were beneath it. The rescue and relief operation was underway.

opening: New Delhi, Two men, aged 60 and 36, are suspected to be trapped under the rubble after a slab of a house under construction collapsed in northeast Delhi's Harsh Vihar area on Sunday, prompting a rescue operation involving the NDRF, fire services and police, officers said.
The incident took place in Milan Garden, triggering panic in the locality as the structure came crashing down.
body: Rescue teams were clearing the debris and making efforts to ascertain whether the two men were trapped underneath, a senior police officer said.
The Delhi Fire Services and police received information about the incident around 7 pm and rushed to the spot.
Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), the local police and the fire department were also engaged in the rescue and relief operation.

A team from the Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) also reached the site and joined the efforts, the officer said." During local inquiries, we learnt that two people who were working at the building may be trapped under the rubble.
One is a 60-year-old man and the other is 36.

Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable," the officer said." Our main focus is to clear all the debris and, if someone is trapped, rescue them quickly," he added.
The officer said construction work was underway on the first floor of the building when the house collapsed.
However, the exact cause of the incident is yet to be ascertained.
As the rescue operation progressed, no one had been found under the debris till the time of filing this report.
Some family members of the two men alleged that the rescue work was progressing slowly and said they were attempting to remove the debris themselves in the hope of locating their relatives.
Police personnel were deployed in strength at the site to maintain law and order and manage the crowd gathered near the collapsed structure.
Emergency responders were coordinating their efforts to clear the debris safely and determine whether anyone remained trapped.
The collapse drew a large number of local residents to the spot, with anxious family members waiting for information about the two men.
Officials said the immediate priority was to clear the debris and establish whether the missing men were beneath it.
The rescue and relief operation was underway.

stories.headline: Tracing 7 decades of J&K Chief Secretaries
stories.title: Tracing 7 decades of J&K Chief Secretaries
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 25: Sajjan Singh Yadav, who is set to become the 34th Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir on November 1, 2026, will inherit a long legacy of Chief Secretaries, both locals and non-locals, with some of them, like Peerzada Ghulam Ahmad, Sheikh Ghulam Rasool, and Ashok Jaitly, having become part of the local folklore. Over the years, J&K’s administrative leadership has evolved despite periods of political instability, central rule, and the region’s transition from a state to a Union Territory in August 2019. The Chief Secretary, the senior-most civil servant in Jammu and Kashmir, is responsible for coordinating the administration, overseeing government departments, and advising the elected government or the administration during periods of central rule. As a result, the Chief Secretary in J&K has always occupied a central position in implementing policy and managing the civil service through these changes. J&K’s longest-serving Chief Secretary, Peerzada Ghulam Ahmad, remained in the hot seat for close to a decade from June 14, 1954, to March 7, 1964, while Ashok Jaitly served as a Chief Secretary from October 9, 1996, to April 30, 2002. Recently, as a Chief Secretary, B V R Subrahmanyam oversaw major transitions, including the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019 and the merger of its former state cadre into the Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territories (AGMUT) cadre in 2021. The Government of India on Saturday, October 24, appointed the 1995-batch AGMUT-cadre officer Sajjan Singh Yadav to succeed Atal Dulloo as the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir, with the change scheduled to take effect from November 1, 2026, or the date Yadav assumes charge, whichever is later. Over the years, some of the Chief Secretaries became part of the local folklore. Peerzada Ghulam Ahmad, a local officer, is one among such Chief Secretaries. He served during the government of Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad, and his tenure coincided with a period of institution-building and expansion of the state administration. The tenure of Pushkar Nath Kaul, who served as a Chief Secretary from March 27, 1977, to January 1, 1978, during Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah’s return to power in 1977, fell within a period of political transition and the restoration of an elected government after central intervention in state politics. The tenure of Syed Muzaffar Aga, who served as a Chief Secretary from January 20, 1978, to April 30, 1980, under Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah’s government, formed part of the administration’s efforts to manage the J&K’s departments and development programmes after the political transition of 1977. Mir Nasrullah, another local, who was the Chief Secretary from January 1, 1984, to January 31, 1986, served during Ghulam Mohammad Shah’s government, which came to power in 1984 after the dismissal of Sheikh Abdullah’s government, and his tenure coincided with a significant political change in the state. Sheikh Ghulam Rasool, a local professor-turned-bureaucrat, served as Chief Secretary from September 21, 1992, to April 5, 1994, during a period of President’s rule and severe political instability associated with the militancy in Jammu and Kashmir, with the administration facing challenges involving law and order, the functioning of government offices, public services, and the restoration of administrative capacity. The tenure of Ashok Jaitley, an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the 1964 batch assigned to the Jammu and Kashmir cadre, who served as a Chief Secretary from October 9, 1996 to April 30, 2002, covered the transition from prolonged central rule to the restoration of an elected government in 1996 when the National Conference (NC) led by Farooq Abdullah returned to office. Jaitley was known for his work in rural development and economic administration. Before his elevation to the top post, he had been associated with reforms in the sericulture sector, including the removal of the state’s monopoly over the marketing of silk. S SBloeria, who hailed from Jammu and served as Chief Secretary from September 30, 2002, to July 31, 2005, succeeded Jaitley and served through the end of Farooq Abdullah’s government and the 2002 Assembly election, which brought a coalition government led by Mufti Mohammad Sayeed to power. Vijay Bakaya, a local Kashmiri Pandit, served as Chief Secretary from August 1, 2005, to May 31, 2006, during Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad’s government. C Phunsog, a Ladakhi officer, served as a Chief Secretary from May 31, 2006, to October 31, 2007, during Azad’s tenure as CM. His appointment placed an officer from Ladakh at the head of the J&K bureaucracy. B R Kundal, who served as a Chief Secretary from November 1, 2007, to June 2, 2008. His appointment came during the final phase of the Congress-led coalition government. Kundal’s tenure was short, and the principal administrative context was continuity in the functioning of government departments ahead of the political upheaval that followed the Amarnath land-transfer controversy in 2008. The tenure of S SKapur, who was Chief Secretary from June 9, 2008, to January 31, 2011, covered the Amarnath land-transfer agitation, the collapse of the Congress-People’s Democratic Party (PDP) coalition in 2008, the Assembly election later that year and the formation of the National Conference-Congress government led by Omar Abdullah in January 2009. Madhav Lal, who was the Chief Secretary from January 31, 2011, to February 18, 2013, served during Omar Abdullah’s government. His period in office followed the 2010 unrest and included efforts by the administration to maintain public services, coordinate development programmes, and respond to the political and security situation. Mohammad Iqbal Khandey, who was the Chief Secretary from February 18, 2013, to August 31, 2015, served during the final years of Omar Abdullah’s first stint as chief minister and the subsequent change of political leadership in 2015. Khandey sought voluntary retirement in 2015 after the National Conference-Congress government completed its term, elections were held in late 2014, and a coalition of the PDP and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) formed a government under Mufti Mohammad Sayeed in March 2015. According to reports, his departure followed differences with the government over frequent transfers of senior officers, highlighting tensions surrounding the management of the civil service and the political executive’s authority over administrative appointments. Braj Raj Sharma, a 1984-batch IAS officer, was the Chief Secretary from August 31, 2015, to April 28, 2017. His tenure covered the death of Chief Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed in January 2016, the subsequent period of Governor’s rule and the formation of a government under Mehbooba Mufti in April 2016. Sharma had previously served as Principal Secretary in the Planning and Development and Home Department and as Chief Electoral Officer during the 2008 Assembly election. During his tenure, the 2016 unrest following the killing of Hizb-ul-Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani presented a major challenge to the civil administration. Bharat Bhushan Vyas, who was Chief Secretary from April 28, 2017, to June 20, 2018, served during the final phase of the PDP-BJP coalition government. The coalition collapsed in June 2018, leading to Governor’s Rule. Vyas’s tenure ended amid another major change in the state’s political administration. His term was also the final period before Jammu and Kashmir’s administration was led by an officer from another state cadre, B V R Subrahmanyam, who served as Chief Secretary from June 20, 2018, to May 30, 2021. Subrahmanyam, a 1987-batch IAS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre, took charge in June 2018 after serving as Additional Chief Secretary (Home) in Chhattisgarh. His tenure covered one of the most consequential administrative changes in J&K’s modern history. On August 5, 2019, the Government of India announced the scrapping of Article 370 and Article 35-A that stripped J&K of its semi-autonomous character. On October 31, 2019, J&K was downgraded from a state into a Union Territory with a legislature, while Ladakh was downgraded into a separate Union Territory without a legislature. The reorganisation involved the division and allocation of administrative responsibilities, assets, employees, institutions, and government functions between the two Union Territories. Subrahmanyam oversaw the coordination of the Union Territory’s administrative machinery during the transition. His tenure also included the period of restrictions and security measures following the August 2019 changes, as well as the transition towards the new Union Territory framework. Arun Kumar Mehta, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, succeeded Subrahmanyam as Chief Secretary from May 31, 2021, to November 30, 2023, after Subrahmanyam moved to the Union Commerce Ministry. Mehta’s tenure covered the consolidation of J&K’s Union Territory administration, the continued implementation of post-2019 governance arrangements, and the integration of the former J&K cadre into the AGMUT cadre in 2021. Atal Dulloo, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the J&K cadre, took over as Chief Secretary on December 1, 2023, and would continue to be in the post till his superannuation on October 31, 2026. Dulloo had served in several departments of J&K, including finance, health, agriculture, and other administrative assignments, before serving as Secretary in the Union Home Ministry’s Department of Border Management. His appointment had brought an officer with extensive experience in J&K back to the top bureaucratic post after central deputation. His tenure covered the return of an elected government under Omar Abdullah following the 2024 Assembly election, the first Assembly election in the Union Territory since the 2019 reorganisation. The administration during his tenure had to coordinate government departments under the Union Territory’s existing constitutional framework while the elected government pursued the restoration of statehood. In October 2026, Dulloo became involved in a public controversy after opposing the introduction of a resolution in the Assembly seeking restoration of statehood. The episode raised questions about the relationship between the elected government and the senior civil service. Sajjan Singh Yadav, a 1995-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, has been appointed to take charge as the 34th Chief Secretary of J&K from November 1, 2026, or the date he assumes charge, whichever is later. Yadav has served in the Delhi administration and the Government of India, including assignments involving public finance, expenditure, public health, and nutrition programmes. However, he has not previously served in J&K.

On August 5, 2019, the Government of India announced the scrapping of Article 370 and Article 35-A that stripped J&K of its semi-autonomous character.
On October 31, 2019, J&K was downgraded from a state into a Union Territory with a legislature, while Ladakh was downgraded into a separate Union Territory without a legislature.
The reorganisation involved the division and allocation of administrative responsibilities, assets, employees, institutions, and government functions between the two Union Territories.
Subrahmanyam oversaw the coordination of the Union Territory’s administrative machinery during the transition.
His tenure also included the period of restrictions and security measures following the August 2019 changes, as well as the transition towards the new Union Territory framework.

Arun Kumar Mehta, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, succeeded Subrahmanyam as Chief Secretary from May 31, 2021, to November 30, 2023, after Subrahmanyam moved to the Union Commerce Ministry.

Mehta’s tenure covered the consolidation of J&K’s Union Territory administration, the continued implementation of post-2019 governance arrangements, and the integration of the former J&K cadre into the AGMUT cadre in 2021.
Atal Dulloo, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the J&K cadre, took over as Chief Secretary on December 1, 2023, and would continue to be in the post till his superannuation on October 31, 2026.

Dulloo had served in several departments of J&K, including finance, health, agriculture, and other administrative assignments, before serving as Secretary in the Union Home Ministry’s Department of Border Management.
His appointment had brought an officer with extensive experience in J&K back to the top bureaucratic post after central deputation.
His tenure covered the return of an elected government under Omar Abdullah following the 2024 Assembly election, the first Assembly election in the Union Territory since the 2019 reorganisation.

The administration during his tenure had to coordinate government departments under the Union Territory’s existing constitutional framework while the elected government pursued the restoration of statehood.
In October 2026, Dulloo became involved in a public controversy after opposing the introduction of a resolution in the Assembly seeking restoration of statehood.
The episode raised questions about the relationship between the elected government and the senior civil service.

Sajjan Singh Yadav, a 1995-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, has been appointed to take charge as the 34th Chief Secretary of J&K from November 1, 2026, or the date he assumes charge, whichever is later.
Yadav has served in the Delhi administration and the Government of India, including assignments involving public finance, expenditure, public health, and nutrition programmes.
However, he has not previously served in J&K.

sentences.text: J&K’s longest-serving Chief Secretary, Peerzada Ghulam Ahmad, remained in the hot seat for close to a decade from June 14, 1954, to March 7, 1964, while Ashok Jaitly served as a Chief Secretary from October 9, 1996, to April 30, 2002.

Sheikh Ghulam Rasool, a local professor-turned-bureaucrat, served as Chief Secretary from September 21, 1992, to April 5, 1994, during a period of President’s rule and severe political instability associated with the militancy in Jammu and Kashmir, with the administration facing challenges involving law and order, the functioning of government offices, public services, and the restoration of administrative capacity.

S SBloeria, who hailed from Jammu and served as Chief Secretary from September 30, 2002, to July 31, 2005, succeeded Jaitley and served through the end of Farooq Abdullah’s government and the 2002 Assembly election, which brought a coalition government led by Mufti Mohammad Sayeed to power.

The tenure of S SKapur, who was Chief Secretary from June 9, 2008, to January 31, 2011, covered the Amarnath land-transfer agitation, the collapse of the Congress-People’s Democratic Party (PDP) coalition in 2008, the Assembly election later that year and the formation of the National Conference-Congress government led by Omar Abdullah in January 2009.

stories.headline: Accident cover for regular Govt employees raised to Rs 1 Crore; over 1 lakh daily wagers left out
stories.title: Accident cover for regular Govt employees raised to Rs 1 Crore; over 1 lakh daily wagers left out
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 25: The Jammu and Kashmir Government’s decision to enhance personal accident insurance coverage for regular employees from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore under a fresh agreement with J&K Bank has raised questions over the disparity in financial protection available to permanent employees and the government’s non-regular workforce. President, Jammu Kashmir Daily Wagers Forum, Sajad Parry, said daily wagers had been left out of the enhanced insurance arrangement and that their long-pending demand for regularisation remained unfulfilled despite repeated promises. “The government has not covered daily wagers under the enhanced insurance scheme. Our demand for regularisation has also not been met despite repeated promises. Thousands of workers have been serving government departments for years, yet they continue to remain without job security and adequate social protection,” Parry said. The five-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed between the Jammu and Kashmir Government and J&K Bank on October 23, raises Group Personal Accident Insurance cover for permanent government employees from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore. The package also provides additional benefits, including disability coverage and financial assistance for eligible family members, subject to applicable terms and conditions. However, the enhanced arrangement has brought renewed attention to the position of more than one lakh casual, daily-rated and other non-regular workers registered across government departments. The government informed the Legislative Assembly that 1,00,501 such workers were registered across departments. Of these, 38,585 were associated with Public Health Engineering, Irrigation and Flood Control, while another 13,616 worked in the Power Development sector. These departments account for more than 52,000 workers, many of whom perform field duties involving electricity networks, water supply, drainage, irrigation and emergency restoration operations. The disparity has raised concerns over the financial security of workers who often face occupational hazards but lack the range of service-related benefits available to permanent employees. The insurance arrangements for daily wagers have changed over the years. While around 12,000 Power Development Department daily wagers were brought under comparable coverage in May 2020, regular employees and daily wagers received Rs 15 lakh in accident insurance protection under arrangements in June 2022. However, when the cover for regular employees was enhanced to Rs 25 lakh in August 2023, daily wagers were excluded from the enhanced arrangement. In June 2026, J&K Bank introduced a separate scheme offering eligible daily-rated, contractual and casual workers Rs 5 lakh in Group Personal Accident Insurance coverage. The latest agreement has now raised the cover for permanent employees to Rs 1 crore, leaving a substantial difference between the two arrangements. The Rs 5 lakh cover available under the separate scheme amounts to one-twentieth of the enhanced insurance available to permanent employees, subject to the respective policy terms and eligibility conditions. The issue also comes against the backdrop of the prolonged demand for regularisation. Daily wagers and casual workers have repeatedly sought a time-bound resolution, arguing that many have continued working in government departments for years without permanent employment status. While regularisation involves legal, administrative and financial considerations, workers’ representatives maintain that their demand for adequate social security should not remain unresolved in the meantime. Permanent government employees may be entitled to service-related benefits such as gratuity, General Provident Fund accumulations and family pension, wherever applicable, besides consideration for compassionate appointment under the relevant rules. Daily wagers generally do not enjoy an equivalent range of assured benefits, although entitlements may vary depending on the applicable schemes and provisions. The disparity has prompted calls for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to intervene and review the insurance arrangements for non-regular workers. The government could initiate discussions with J&K Bank to explore extending comparable accident insurance and disability protection to eligible daily wagers, casual labourers and other non-regular employees through a supplementary agreement or a separate comprehensive scheme. For workers who have spent years serving government departments without regularisation, adequate insurance protection could provide an important financial safeguard for their families in the event of accidental death or disability. The central question remains whether workers’ families should face substantially different levels of financial protection because of the employment status of their breadwinners.
